extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and OPQA (Office Patent Quality Assurance) reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: A structured OPQA (MRF) questionnaire for assessing whether 35 U.S.C. 112(a)/(b)/(d) rejections in an office action are procedurally and substantively compliant. Reviewers record claim-level findings, reasons for noncompliance, characteristics, feedback, and possible accolades.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(a) Written Description - compliance determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Were all the 35 U.S.C. 112(a) Written Description rejection(s) in compliance? (Yes/No). Determination based on the rejection properly identifying the claim(s), the statute (including subparagraphs), and being supported by sufficient evidence to support the conclusion of lack of sufficient written description of the claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a 112(a) rejection was made, answer Yes or No. Consult the statutory compliance standard and scenarios for assistance. If Yes, proceed to question for accolades; if No, proceed to identify noncompliant claims and explain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify claims with non-compliant 112(a) rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: List each claim discussed individually as a basis for the noncompliance and include dependent claims which inherit the noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each claim must be discussed individually in an 'Explanation of Noncompliance' section. Include dependent claims that inherit noncompliance. Use claim numbering and tie explanations to specific claim limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(a) Noncompliance root - limitation origin (independent/dependent/both)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the noncompliance is directed to limitations introduced in: (a) Only the independent claim(s); (b) Only the dependent claim(s); or (c) Both the independent and dependent claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check only one box based on where the limitation that is the basis for the noncompliance first appears in the claim tree. Examples provided illustrate independent-only, dependent-only, and mixed-origin situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of another compliant 112(a) Written Description basis
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims identified as having a noncompliant 112(a) rejection, was another compliant 112(a) Written Description rejection applied? (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An individual claim may be rejected under 112(a) on multiple bases; if every claim with a noncompliant basis also has another compliant basis, answer Yes. If even one claim lacks any compliant basis, answer No. Consult 'MRF In-part Instruction' for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(a) Noncompliance reason: failure to properly identify claim(s)/statute (4a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection(s) does not properly identify the rejected claim(s) and/or identify the correct statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check 4(a) when claim identification or statute/subparagraph identification is the basis for noncompliance. Do not check 4(a) for insufficient evidence issues. Do not use 4(a) to capture omitted rejections. Explanation should focus on basis related to identification only; avoid rhetorical questions and personalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(a) Noncompliance reason: insufficient evidence inventor lacked possession (4b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection(s) does not provide sufficient evidence as to why applicant did not have possession of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult statutory compliance scenarios to determine sufficiency of evidence. If 4(b) is checked, at least one of 4(b)(i)-4(b)(iii) must be checked. Explanation should be focused, avoid rhetorical questions and personalization, and be consistent with boxes checked under 4(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(a) 4(b)(i) - insufficient evidence that amended/new limitations lack support (new matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection does not provide sufficient evidence to support the conclusion that the amended or newly added claim limitations lack support in the original disclosure (i.e., new matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If asserted new matter actually has support in the original disclosure, indicate which source(s) of support apply: A. Original claim(s); B. Original drawing(s); C. Original specification through express, implicit or inherent disclosure. Use these boxes to identify the nature of the incorrect new-matter finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(a) 4(b)(ii) - new matter only in specification that doesn't change claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The new matter was added only to the specification and does not change the scope of the claimed invention and therefore does not necessitate a rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the alleged new matter appears solely in the specification and does not alter claim scope; explain why the added specification content does not create new matter for the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(a) 4(b)(iii) - insufficient evidence inventor lacks possession of originally claimed invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection does not provide sufficient evidence to support the conclusion that the inventor lacks possession of the originally claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the examiner's evidence does not reasonably establish lack of possession of the originally-claimed invention; tie explanation to the record and disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(a) Explanation style guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: How the reviewer should write explanation entries for noncompliance related to identification and/or insufficient evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only include comments directed to the specific basis for noncompliance. Avoid rhetorical questioning and personalization; the write-up should be an assessment of the work product and should provide a reasoned explanation consistent with the boxes checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(a) Additional information/feedback categories (5a-5g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional feedback boxes to indicate additional characteristics or root causes related to the noncompliance (check all that apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boxes include: 5a analysis more appropriate for lack of enablement; 5b analysis primarily questions to applicant rather than analysis of written description; 5c noncompliance due to unreasonable claim interpretation (only if rejection indicates how limitation is construed); 5d 112(f)-related; 5e lack of sufficient algorithm for CII; 5f related to deposit of biological material; 5g None of the above. Comments must support reasoning for boxes checked; do not guess root cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(a) Comments / suggestions / best practices (Q6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional comments the reviewer may provide that are not directed to the basis of a noncompliance. May include suggestions, feedback, or best practices for the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not repeat issues that form the basis of a noncompliance (those belong under Question 4). Best practices and suggestions are optional and should be constructive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 112(a) Written Description rejection(s) (Q7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist of characteristics that may be exemplified in 112(a) rejections; reviewer checks all that apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include: addresses substantially all claims individually (limited claim lumping); provides citations to relevant portions of the specification and thorough explanation of lack of possession; sets forth a claim interpretation that indicates how the examiner is construing the claim/term/phrase; included detailed legal analysis referencing case law/policy; included appropriate suggestions to overcome the rejection (not generic FP language); None of the above. Checking indicates presence of a characteristic — it does not assess accuracy or accolade-worthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(a) Accolade eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there an accolade related to 112(a) Written Description rejection(s)? (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accolades may be proposed only if all 112(a) rejections were compliant AND at least one characteristic box is appropriately checked (i.e., 'none of the above' not checked). Consult current accolade procedures and guidance for wording and eligibility. Complete the provided sentence per guidance when indicating Yes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(b) Indefiniteness - compliance determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Were all the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejection(s) in compliance? (Yes/No). Determination based on proper identification of claim(s), statute (including subparagraphs), and sufficient evidence to support conclusion of indefiniteness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a 112(b) rejection was made, update the answer to Yes or No. Consult statutory compliance standard and scenarios. If Yes, proceed to accolade question; if No, go to identify noncompliant claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify claims with non-compliant 112(b) rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: List each claim discussed individually as a basis for the noncompliance and include dependent claims which inherit the noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each claim discussed must be tied to the 'Explanation of Noncompliance' and dependent claims inheriting the defect must be listed. Use the claim-tree approach to determine origin of limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(b) Noncompliance root - limitation origin (independent/dependent/both)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the noncompliance is directed to limitations introduced in independent claims, dependent claims, or both (check only one).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is based on where the limitation that is the basis for the noncompliance first appears in the claim tree. Examples provided to illustrate proper selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of another compliant 112(b) basis
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims with noncompliant 112(b) bases, determine whether another compliant 112(b) rejection basis was applied to the same claim(s). (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If every claim with a noncompliant basis also has another compliant basis, answer Yes. If even one claim lacks any compliant basis, answer No. Examples illustrate mixed-basis scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(b) Noncompliance reason: failure to properly identify claim(s)/statute (4a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection(s) does not properly identify the rejected claim(s) and/or identify the correct statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when claim identification or statute/subparagraph identification is the basis for noncompliance. Do not check 4(a) for insufficient evidence issues, or for omitted rejections (raise as omitted 112(b) rejection). Explanation should be focused and not personalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(b) Noncompliance reason: insufficient evidence of indefiniteness (4b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection(s) does not provide sufficient evidence that the claim(s) does not particularly point out and distinctly claim that which the inventor regards as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 4(b) is checked, identify at least one of 4(b)(i)-4(b)(iii): i) rejection did not point out the specific term/phrase that is indefinite; ii) rejection did not provide sufficient reasoning to support the conclusion of indefiniteness; iii) rejection did not provide sufficient reasoning that the claims are not drawn to that which the inventor regards as the invention. Note that 112(b) has two separate requirements (MPEP 2171) and there is a presumption the claims are directed to what the inventor regards as the invention (MPEP 2172).

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(b) Noncompliance issues list (5a-5k)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific issue categories that may relate to noncompliance under 112(b); reviewer must check at least one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include: a. Breadth versus indefiniteness; b. Relative terminology; c. Ranges and amounts limitations; d. Exemplary language (e.g., 'for example'); e. Lack of antecedent basis; f. Functional language; g. Alternative limitations (e.g., Markush group); h. Unclaimed/omitted essential subject matter; i. 112(b) is related to 112(f); j. Unbound functional claiming; k. Other (specify). Check all that apply and support with explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(b) Additional information/feedback (6a-6c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Boxes to capture additional feedback reasons for noncompliance under 112(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: 6a rejection only based on specification without basis in claim terminology; 6b noncompliance result of unreasonable claim interpretation (only when rejection indicates how claim is being construed); 6c none of the above. Comments must support checked boxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(b) Comments / suggestions / best practices (Q7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional suggestions or feedback to benefit the examiner not directed to the basis of noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep comments constructive and separate from the formal 'Explanation of Noncompliance' in Question 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 112(b) Rejection(s) (Q8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist of characteristics that may be exemplified in 112(b) rejections; check all that apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options mirror 112(a): addresses substantially all claims individually (limited claim lumping); provides citations to the specification and explains why claim does not particularly point out and distinctly claim the invention; sets forth claim interpretation (e.g., BRI, special definitions); included detailed legal analysis and case law/policy; included appropriate suggestions to overcome rejection(s); none of the above. Checking indicates presence of a characteristic, not an endorsement of accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(b) Accolade eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there an accolade related to 112(b) Rejection(s)? (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accolades may be proposed only if rejections were compliant and characteristics justify an accolade. Consult accolade procedures; complete required sentence when indicating Yes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(d) Improper dependent claim - compliance determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Were all the 35 U.S.C. 112(d) rejection(s) in compliance? (Yes/No). Determination based on proper identification of claim(s), statute (including subparagraphs), and sufficient evidence to support the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a 112(d) rejection was made, update Yes or No. Consult statutory compliance standard and scenarios. If No, identify noncompliant claims and proceed to explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify claims with non-compliant 112(d) rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: List each claim discussed individually as a basis for the noncompliance and include dependent claims which inherit the noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each claim discussion must be tied to the 'Explanation of Noncompliance.' Use claim-tree logic to determine where the problematic limitation originates.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(d) Noncompliance root - limitation origin (independent/dependent/both)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the noncompliance is directed to limitations introduced in independent claims, dependent claims, or both (check only one).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select based on where the limitation forming the basis for noncompliance first appears in the claim tree; examples illustrate selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of another compliant 112(d) basis
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims with noncompliant 112(d) bases, was another compliant 112(d) rejection applied? (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An individual claim may have multiple 112(d) bases; if every claim with a noncompliant basis also has another compliant basis, answer Yes. Otherwise answer No.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(d) Noncompliance reason: failure to properly identify claim(s)/statute (4a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection(s) does not properly identify the rejected claim(s) and/or identify the correct statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check 4(a) where identification of claim(s) or statute/subparagraph is the basis for noncompliance. Do not use 4(a) to capture omitted rejections. Explanation should be focused on identification issues and avoid personalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(d) Noncompliance reason: insufficient evidence to support the 112(d) rejection (4b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection(s) does not provide sufficient evidence to support the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 4(b) is checked, identify at least one: 4(b)(i) the rejection does not provide sufficient evidence that the claim(s) does not specify a further limitation of the subject matter of the claim from which it depends; 4(b)(ii) the rejection does not provide sufficient evidence that the claim(s) does not include all of the limitations of the claim from which it depends. Provide reasoned explanation consistent with boxes checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(d) Additional information/feedback (5a-5d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback boxes for root causes related to 112(d) noncompliance (check all that apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: 5a rejection should have been made under 112(b); 5b noncompliance is result of unreasonable claim interpretation (check only when rejection shows how a limitation is construed); 5c rejection improperly based on the patentable significance of the further limitation; 5d none of the above. Support choices with explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(d) Comments / suggestions / best practices (Q6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional comments the reviewer may provide that are not directed to the basis of a noncompliance. May include suggestions or best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep comments constructive and separate from formal noncompliance explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 112(d) Rejection(s) (Q7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist of characteristics that may be exemplified in 112(d) rejections; check all that apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include: addresses substantially all claims individually (limited claim lumping); sets forth a claim interpretation for purposes of the rejection; included detailed legal analysis and applicable case law/policy; included appropriate suggestions to overcome rejection(s); None of the above. Checking indicates presence of characteristic only.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(d) Accolade eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there an accolade related to 112(d) Rejection(s)? (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accolades should not be proposed if any rejections under 112(d) were noncompliant or if 'none of the above' is checked for characteristics. Consult accolade procedures when indicating Yes and complete required sentence.
